question: The Age of Consent Act, 1891 increased the minimum marriage age for girls from:
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 to 12 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Age of Consent Act, 1891, was a landmark legislation passed during British rule in India to increase the minimum age for marriage for girls.
 
• The act raised the minimum age of marriage for girls from **10 years to 12 years**, aiming to address issues of child marriage and protect young girls.
 
• It was enacted following widespread criticism of the practice of child marriage and sexual exploitation of young girls in society during that period.
 
• Reform movements, such as those led by Indian social reformers including **Behramji Malabari**, played a significant role in advocating for this legal change.
 
• The legislation specifically targeted the age of consent for marital relations, ensuring that girls below the age of 12 could not legally consent to such relations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 10 to 11 years**

 
 
• There was no historical evidence or legislation during British India that increased the minimum marriage age for girls from 10 to 11 years.
 
• This option is incorrect as the Age of Consent Act, 1891, explicitly raised the age from 10 to 12 years.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: 10 to 13 years**
 
 
• While there were later reforms in the 20th century that further increased the marriage age for girls, the Age of Consent Act, 1891, set the age at 12 years.
 
• This option does not align with the historical timeline of the act.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 10 to 14 years**
 
 
• The Age of Consent Act, 1891, did not set the minimum marriage age for girls at 14 years.
 
• Further amendments and legal reforms in India raised the marriage age for girls in later years, but this was not part of the 1891 legislation.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Child Marriage and Social Reforms in Colonial India**
 
 
• The Age of Consent Act, 1891, was part of broader social reforms during British rule in India to tackle child marriage, which was prevalent in society.
 
• Efforts by social reformers such as **Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Behramji Malabari** were critical in initiating discussions around women’s rights and child welfare.
 
• These reforms were also influenced by growing awareness and pressure from international human rights movements.
